concepts.quote: if (arr[i] == key) return i; else return -1;
concepts.why: The if-else is valid Java, but putting return -1 in the else branch ends the search at the first non-matching element, and returning i on the first match finds the first occurrence, not the last. This is a logic error, not a wrong rule about Java.
Uses arr[i] correctly to get the element at position i, but does not reason about index values or bounds.
Writes a correct comparison expression that gives a boolean, but never evaluates it.
Names a for loop but leaves the header out, so it shows no initialization, condition or update, and no pass order such as a backward scan for the last occurrence.
